name: C2b1a (M401)
description: Haplogroup C2b1a (C-M401) is the core Mongolic branch of C2b1 and the direct ancestor of the 'Star Cluster' (C2b1a1-F3918) associated with Genghis Khan and the Borjigin dynasty. C2b1a is strongly concentrated in Mongolia, among Buryats, and in the Mongolian-speaking populations of China (Inner Mongolia). It splits into two subclades: C2b1a1, the famous Star Cluster lineage that expanded explosively in the 13th century CE, and C2b1a2 (Z22424), a sister clade found among Mongolian populations that did not participate in the same founder effect. The MRCA of C2b1a lived approximately 4,000 BCE — several thousand years before Genghis Khan — indicating a deep prehistorical origin for Mongolic paternal lineages on the Mongolian plateau.
interestingFact: The extraordinary diversity within C2b1a reveals that the Mongolian plateau was home to a significant C2b1a-carrying population for thousands of years before Genghis Khan — the 13th-century explosion of C2b1a1 (Star Cluster) was not the origin of Mongolic lineages, but the final and most extreme episode in a long history of C2b1a dominance on the steppe.

clans.name: House of Borjigin
clans.note: Ruling clan of the Mongol Empire; C2b1a1 is proposed as their patrilineal marker

clans.name: Khalka Mongols
clans.note: Dominant ethnic group of Mongolia; high C2b1a frequency
